summary: Root cause is cfg-2207: the cost-optimisation profile 'small' applied at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z cut portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5, exhausting the Hikari pool and stalling /v1/portfolio/*, which surfaced at api-gateway as upstream-timeout 504s (confidence 0.78, high). The chain is directly observed: pool usage pinned at 5.0 (active=5=total, idle=0, waiting=43) with explicit 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' errors, simultaneous with portfolio-service p99 jumping from ~180ms to ~4.2s at 09:52-09:54 and gateway p99 stepping from ~200ms to ~4.3s. The reported suspect — the 08:00Z envoy 1.30 / HTTP-2-to-upstream deploy — is effectively excluded: it preceded onset by 1h48m with no latent step, and order-service, the other h2 upstream from the same deploy, stayed flat (p99 ~149ms, error ~0.2%) throughout. The gateway is the propagation surface, not the origin; shared components ledger-db and redis-cache show no degradation signal at onset.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service DB connection pool cut to 5 (cfg-2207) exhausts the pool, stalling /v1/portfolio/* and surfacing as gateway 504s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A cost-optimisation profile 'small' applied at 09:52Z reduced portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 (cfg-2207). The pool (HikariPool-1) had been running at ~12 connections against a 50-slot pool with zero saturation, and never saturated on the old pool. Immediately after the cut it pins at the new ceiling of 5 (active=5=total, idle=0, waiting=43), requests block on JDBC acquisition and exceed the 3000ms timeout, portfolio-service returns 503/slow responses, and api-gateway's upstream calls to portfolio-service time out, producing the p99 step change and 504s on /v1/portfolio/*. The gateway is the propagation surface, not the origin.

causal_chain.claim: infra-automation applies profile 'small' to portfolio-service datasource: db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 at 09:52:00Z
Pre-cut the pool was healthy: db_pool_in_use steady ~11.5-12.7 on a 50-slot pool through 09:52, no pre-cut elevation, no saturation (active never near 50)
At 1-min granularity the pool metric steps 11.89 -> 5.0 between 09:52 and 09:53, i.e. the ceiling change takes effect exactly at the config apply
Immediately after, the pool pins at the new ceiling: total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43; waiting counts collapse onto the 5-slot pool
Threads block on connection acquisition and hit 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' / 'Connection is not available... after 3000ms'; first ERROR 09:53:19Z
portfolio-service's own latency step and 5xx onset follow within ~1-2 min (p99 elevated in the 09:52 bucket; error_rate first elevated 09:54 bucket, ~22%)
Gateway calls to the slow portfolio-service exceed upstream timeout -> single signature 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504' (first 09:53:53Z)
Gateway p99 steps from ~207ms to ~3.1-4.3s and error_rate from ~0.2% to ~7.2%; users see portfolio page timeouts and 504s
Same failure shape (wrong profile overriding pool size -> pool exhausted -> timeouts, no reset/refused signature) as HIST-115

assumptions: Config changed_at 09:52:00Z reflects runtime apply within ~1 min; the pool metric step (F27) and the simultaneous p99 step (F30) support this despite F8's coarse 3-min onset window placing onset in 09:48-09:51.
A 5-connection pool is structurally insufficient for portfolio-service's normal load, which the waiting=43 / total=5 evidence implies.

The ~12-connection pre-cut level is normal-but-under-high-concurrency (per-request connection holding time means ~12 in use at any instant corresponds to far higher concurrent request demand), so cutting the ceiling to 5 strangles it even though instantaneous in-use was only ~12.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Gateway envoy 1.30 / HTTP-2-to-upstream upgrade (dep-5220) causes upstream stalls on portfolio-service, producing p99 step change and 504s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 08:00Z gateway release dep-5220 changed the envoy filter chain and enabled HTTP/2 to both the portfolio-service and order-service upstreams (envoy 1.29->1.30). Multiplexing / max-concurrent-streams behaviour with the portfolio upstream stalls requests, so gateway p99 rises through the roof and /v1/portfolio/* returns 504s, echoing HIST-116. The best evidence against this is scope: order-service, which also received h2 from the same deploy, shows no deviation at all.

causal_chain.claim: platform-team deploys dep-5220 at 08:00Z: envoy 1.29->1.30, upstream protocol h2 enabled for portfolio-service AND order-service
HTTP/2 multiplexing/max-streams behaviour degrades upstream connections to portfolio-service (analogue of HIST-116)
Requests stall on the gateway->portfolio-service hop, gateway p99 climbs and /v1/portfolio/holdings requests time out to 504
Users see portfolio page spinning and timing out

assumptions: Envoy 1.30 vs portfolio-service h2 negotiation can produce stalls for this workload and the effect could be latent (~1h48m) rather than immediate — untested because no data covers 08:00-09:48Z gateway/portfolio latency.
A h2 fault on the shared upstream protocol could somehow affect only the portfolio-service h2 upstream and not the order-service h2 upstream, despite both being enabled by the same deploy.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation: gateway/upstream throughput trend outgrows provisioned capacity, no single triggering change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Gradual traffic growth or accumulated connection churn saturates the request path until request handling exceeds timeout budgets, producing the p99 step and 504s. No single change is the trigger; load simply outgrew provisioned capacity.

causal_chain.claim: Traffic/connection demand grows on the /v1/portfolio/* path
Request path saturates and requests exceed timeout budgets

assumptions: Assumes load grew, contrary to the flat request_rate (~1232-1294 req/s) and flat CPU (F10); and contrary to the flat portfolio latency up to 09:50Z (F28).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared-component fault: ledger-db failover/saturation (or redis-cache) on the portfolio path stalls portfolio-service then the gateway
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared (multi-tenant) component on the /v1/portfolio/* path — ledger-db (also used by order-service and payment-service) or redis-cache (also used by auth-service and market-data-service) — degraded near 09:50Z, slowing portfolio-service's DB/cache calls until its connection pool saturated, and the gateway 504s are the propagation surface. This is now strongly contradicted: ledger-db shows no failover/saturation/latency/CPU signal, replication lag and CPU flat, slow queries flat, and its connections_active actually drops across onset.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db or redis-cache on the portfolio path degrades/fails over near 09:50Z
portfolio-service DB/cache calls slow, holding connections longer until its pool saturates
portfolio-service responses exceed gateway upstream timeout; gateway p99 steps and 504s appear

assumptions: No change/deploy on shared components in window (F16) does not preclude spontaneous failover; but ledger-db telemetry (F31/F32/F33) now actively contradicts it.
redis-cache saturation remains only unsupported by absence of error logs — its health metrics were never retrieved (F35).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Superseded by telemetry: ledger-db shows no failover, saturation, latency or CPU signal at onset (F31: replication_lag and cpu flat; F32: slow_queries flat and connections_active actually DROPS after 09:45; F33: single unrelated WARN at 07:15Z), and redis-cache shows only benign /internal/metrics WARNs with nothing clustering at 09:50Z (F34). Also, the pool failure appears only AFTER the 09:52 ceiling cut, with zero pre-cut saturation (F27), inconsistent with a backend slowdown driving pool exhaustion.

facts.statement: Portfolio-service config cfg-2207 reduced db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z, applied by infra-automation with description 'Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource'; it is the closest change in time to the 09:48-09:51Z gateway onset and to the 09:53:19Z first pool-exhaustion error.

portfolio-service shows DB connection-pool exhaustion concurrent with the incident: 503 errors first matching at 09:53:19Z with signatures 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' (270 occurrences) and 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43)' (233 occurrences, first_seen 09:54:29Z).

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was steady at ~11.5-12.7 connections on the 50-slot pool from 08:00Z through 09:52Z, then stepped down to exactly 5.0 at 09:53 and stayed there; at 1-minute granularity there is zero pre-cut pool elevation (09:51=11.75, 09:52=11.89, 09:53=5.0).

portfolio-service latency_p99 was flat/normal ~173-189ms from 08:00Z to 09:50Z with no elevation; the first elevated bucket is 09:52 (avg 2211.8ms, max 4250.91ms) and then steady ~4-4.5s. Its error_rate was normal ~0.14-0.28% through 09:52Z and first elevated at 09:54 (22.3%).

api-gateway p99 latency shows a step change from a ~200-215ms baseline to multi-second values: 09:40=206.74ms, 09:50=3119.97ms, 10:00=4328.65ms, holding ~4300ms through 11:50; gateway error_rate steps from ~0.17-0.25% to 4.44% at 09:50 and steady ~7.1-7.4% from 10:00 onward.

The gateway error signature is a single pattern, 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504' (252 WARN occurrences, first 09:53:53Z, last 11:58:44Z); no order-service, payment-service or other upstream route appears — this is a timeout, not connection-refused or reset.

portfolio-service mirrors the gateway degradation: error_rate steps from 5.04% avg in the 09:40 bucket / ~0.2% baseline to 22.46% at 09:58 and holds 21.6-22.5% through 11:46; latency_p99 goes from 1291.3ms at 09:40 to 4213.59ms at 09:58 and ~4100-4200ms thereafter.

The suspect gateway deploy dep-5220 (v9.3.0, envoy 1.29->1.30, HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service upstreams) was deployed at 08:00:00Z, ~1h48m before the first gateway latency jump at 09:51Z, and remained live (rolled_back_at null) with no intermediate gateway change.

order-service, which also received HTTP/2 from the same 08:00Z deploy, was unaffected: error_rate stayed 0.18-0.23% in every bucket 08:00-11:46Z and latency_p99 stayed flat at ~149-152ms across 09:40-11:46Z; a gateway-level HTTP/2 fault shared by both h2 upstreams would be expected to touch order-service too.
Gateway CPU and request rate stayed flat across onset (cpu_pct ~41-43%, request_rate ~1232-1293 req/s), ruling out gateway CPU saturation or a traffic surge.

ledger-db shows no failover, saturation, latency or CPU signal around 09:50Z: replication_lag_ms flat ~39.4-40.7ms (max 44.8ms at 08:00Z), cpu_pct flat ~29.4-30.6%, slow_queries_per_min ~0.94-1.19/min, and connections_active actually drops after 09:45 (57.95 -> 54.49) rather than queueing.

ledger-db WARN logs for 06:00-11:59Z contain exactly one entry (07:15:46Z, 'slow request 2439ms on /internal/metrics', unrelated) with no DB/connection/failover errors; redis-cache WARN logs contain only 3 benign '/internal/metrics' entries spread across the window with nothing clustering at 09:50Z.

Widening the portfolio-service change history to 2026-03-01T00:00Z-2026-03-10T11:59Z returns only one config change (cfg-2207) and zero deployments, so no earlier same-service change can explain onset; the window as a whole contains exactly three changes (order-service log.sampling_rate only, and cfg-2207), with zero changes in the 2026-03-09T18:00Z-06:00Z pre-window baseline.

The error signature (upstream timeout, no reset/refused) matches precedent HIST-115 ('order-service connection pool misconfiguration', resolution 'Reverted config') rather than HIST-116 ('HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade', resolution 'Rolled back gateway').

assumptions: Assumption: the recorded cfg-2207 changed_at 09:52:00Z reflects runtime apply within ~1 minute; the pool metric step (F27) and the near-simultaneous portfolio p99 step (F30) support this, though the gateway's 3-min bucket onset window (09:48-09:51, F8) leaves ~1 bucket of ordering ambiguity.

Assumption: a 5-connection pool is structurally insufficient for portfolio-service's normal load; this is implied by waiting=43 with total=5 (F12), but per-request connection-hold time at the pre-cut ~12 connections was never measured.

Assumption: the ~12-connection pre-cut level was normal for the service under high concurrency (many short-lived acquisitions), so cutting the ceiling to 5 strangled it even though instantaneous in-use was only ~12.

Assumption: the 08:00Z deploy's effect, if any, would have appeared promptly rather than latent ~1h48m; no data covers 08:00-09:48Z gateway/portfolio latency, so latency in that gap is assumed flat based on the 09:40 bucket being at baseline.

Assumption: absence of redis-cache error logs indicates redis-cache was healthy; its health metrics (hit_ratio_pct, evictions_per_min, memory_pct, connected_clients) were never retrieved (F35), so redis-cache saturation is unsupported but not positively excluded.

Assumption: the gateway log sample's single top_pattern (count 252 = total_matched) means no meaningful non-portfolio timeout lines exist, despite both gateway log queries returning truncated=true (40 of 252 rows returned).

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Within the 09:52-09:54Z window all at 1-2 min resolution: the pool metric switches 11.89->5.0 at 09:53, portfolio-service p99 is already spiking in the 09:52 bucket, and portfolio-service 5xx first appear at 09:54 — effectively simultaneous with the 09:52:00Z config apply.

timeline.event: Gateway deploy dep-5220 (v9.3.0, envoy 1.29->1.30, HTTP/2 enabled to portfolio-service and order-service upstreams) goes live.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use steady at ~12 connections on the 50-slot pool; no pre-cut pool elevation.
Gateway p99 still at baseline 206.74ms, error_rate ~0.17-0.25%; portfolio-service p99 ~173-189ms and error_rate ~0.14-0.28% — all normal.
Gateway p99 normal on 3-min buckets (206.71ms); onset occurs between 09:48 and 09:51.

Config cfg-2207 applies: portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 ('cost-optimisation profile small'). Pool metric still reads 11.89 in the 09:52 bucket; portfolio-service p99 begins spiking in the 09:52 bucket (avg 2211.8ms).
Pool metric steps down sharply to 5.0 and pins there; 09:53:19Z first portfolio-service 503 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms'.
First api-gateway WARN 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504'.
portfolio-service error_rate first elevated to 22.3% and stays ~21.5-23.2%; HikariPool 'total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43' signature first seen 09:54:29Z.
Gateway p99 ~4328.65ms and error_rate steady ~7.1-7.4%; portfolio-service p99 ~4213.59ms; degradation persists un-recovered.
Incident INC-002 reported by on-call SRE (13 minutes after cfg-2207 applied), with the 08:00Z gateway upgrade suspected.
Latest data: gateway p99 still ~4.3s, error_rate ~7.2%, portfolio-service error_rate ~21.6-22.5%; incident unresolved. order-service, ledger-db and redis-cache all remain flat/unaffected throughout.

recommended_actions.action: Revert config change cfg-2207 on portfolio-service: restore db.pool.max_size from 5 to 50 (or remove the 'small' cost-optimisation profile from the service datasource) and force a runtime apply/pod restart if the pool does not resize in place.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 is the sole portfolio-service change in ten days and the closest change to onset; the pool pins at exactly 5 with active=5=total, idle=0, waiting=43 and 3000ms acquisition timeouts (F12, F13, F17, F26, F27). Restoring the known-good ceiling of 50 directly removes the constraint causing the timeouts.

recommended_actions.action: After the revert, confirm recovery on the same signals: portfolio-service db_pool_in_use returning above 5 without hitting a ceiling, portfolio-service p99 back to ~173-189ms and error_rate to ~0.2%, and gateway p99 returning to ~200ms with error_rate back to ~0.2% and 504s ceasing.
recommended_actions.rationale: This closes the one remaining gap — no positive 'revert restores service' confirmation exists — and is the cheapest discriminator against the residual alternative cause (dep-5220). Full recovery on revert confirms H1; failure to recover would reopen H2.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back gateway deploy dep-5220 as the first action; keep it live while the cfg-2207 revert is evaluated, and only roll it back if the revert does not restore p99/504s.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5220 is 1h48m before onset with no latent step, and order-service (the other h2 upstream from the same deploy) shows no deviation at all (p99 ~149ms, error ~0.2%), which contradicts a shared HTTP/2 fault on the gateway (F14, F20, F21, F24).

recommended_actions.action: Gate or block the 'small' cost-optimisation profile from being applied to any service datasource until it is load-tested: add an admission check that rejects db.pool.max_size reductions below a service-appropriate floor.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure was a wrong environment/profile override of a datasource pool size, matching HIST-115 ('Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', resolution 'Reverted config'); the same automation (infra-automation) applied this profile unconditionally (F5, F13).

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on portfolio-service DB pool saturation (active == total, idle == 0, waiting > 0 for N minutes) and on JDBC acquisition-timeout rate, and instrument Hikari active/idle/waiting/total as first-class metrics since only db_pool_in_use is currently exposed.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool's saturation and waiter count were observable only in application logs (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43) and portfolio-service exposes no hikaricp_* metrics (F12, F25), which is why the incident was detected via gateway 504s rather than at the pool.

recommended_actions.action: Require a sizing review and canary stage for cost-optimisation config profiles before fleet-wide apply, including a minimum-headroom rule derived from observed peak db_pool_in_use per service.
recommended_actions.rationale: portfolio-service was steady at ~12 connections against a 50-slot pool with zero saturation history, so the cut removed ~4x headroom instantly; a headroom rule derived from observed usage would have blocked a 50->5 change (F26, F27, F5).

recommended_actions.action: Add a route/upstream-tagged error and latency metric on api-gateway (per-route 504 counts and p99) so route scope is measurable directly instead of inferred from log labels.
recommended_actions.rationale: The conclusion that degradation is confined to /v1/portfolio/* was established indirectly from gateway log upstream labels and upstream metrics because api-gateway exposes only aggregate cpu_pct/error_rate/latency_p99_ms/memory_pct/request_rate/restarts.

data_gaps: No metric/trace data covers 08:00-09:48Z gateway/portfolio latency, so it cannot be directly shown that no latent step followed the 08:00Z deploy; the gap is bridged only by the 09:40 bucket sitting at baseline (F28) and by order-service being flat (F20, F21).

Gateways logs were truncated in both queries (40 of 252 matching rows returned), so a small number of non-portfolio upstream timeout lines outside the returned sample cannot be mechanically excluded; top_patterns showing count 252 = total_matched makes this unlikely.

redis-cache health metrics (hit_ratio_pct, evictions_per_min, memory_pct, connected_clients) were never retrieved due to tool-budget exhaustion (F35), so redis-cache saturation cannot be positively excluded — only unsupported by the absence of error logs.

ledger-db exposes no p99/query-latency metric and no failover/audit log at INFO level was checked (only WARN filtering), so a silent INFO-level failover is not 100% excluded even though replication_lag and CPU are flat (F31, F32, F33).

No sub-120s granularity exists for portfolio-service p99/error_rate, so the ordering of the pool step vs the gateway p99 jump retains ~1 bucket ambiguity (09:48-09:51 gateway onset vs 09:52 apply); the finest evidence is log first-match 09:53:19Z pool error vs 09:53:53Z gateway 504.

Whether the pre-cut ~12-connection level was a stable long-run level or a recent rise was not measured (pool utilization before 08:00Z not queried), so it cannot be ruled out that pool pressure was gradually building before the cut.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Reverting cfg-2207 (pool back to 50) fails to restore gateway p99, portfolio-service p99 and 504 rate to baseline — this would invalidate H1 and reopen H2/the gateway upgrade.
Evidence that gateway/portfolio latency already stepped at or shortly after 08:00Z (a latent-then-persistent step from dep-5220), which no data currently covers, would shift weight to H2.
Detection of a connection reset/refused signature (rather than upstream timeout) on the gateway for portfolio-service, matching HIST-116's HTTP/2 envoy upgrade shape, would support H2 (F4, F15).
Retrieval of redis-cache health metrics showing a hit-ratio collapse or eviction spike beginning ~09:50Z would support a shared-component contribution.
Evidence that order-service (or another h2 upstream from dep-5220) also degraded on the h2 route after 08:00Z would undercut the scope-based exclusion of H2 (F20, F21, F24).
A confirmed pool-size apply time materially earlier than 09:52:00Z (e.g. runtime apply at ~09:49Z) would remove the residual 09:48-09:51 versus 09:52 ordering tension in favor of H1 more strongly.

findings.statement: The suspect gateway upgrade dep-5220 (v9.3.0, envoy 1.29->1.30, HTTP/2 to portfolio/order upstreams) was deployed at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z, ~1h48m BEFORE the first gateway latency jump at 09:51Z, and remains live (rolled_back_at null). No intermediate gateway change exists between 08:00Z and the 09:48-09:51Z onset.

The gateway failure signature is an upstream timeout, not a connection reset: 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504' (first 09:53:53Z). This matches HIST-115's 'connection is not available'/'pool exhausted' shape (config_change via wrong profile) rather than HIST-116's HTTP/2 resets from an envoy upgrade — no reset/refused signature was observed on the gateway.

Shared components on the /v1/portfolio/* path are ledger-db (shared=true) and redis-cache (shared=true); portfolio-service also calls market-data-service, which reaches redis-cache and exchange-gateway. Neither shared component has any config change or deployment in the 06:00-11:59Z window.

Widening the portfolio-service baseline to 2026-03-01T00:00Z-2026-03-10T11:59Z still returns only one config change (cfg-2207) and zero deployments — the pool cut is the sole portfolio-service change in ten days, so no earlier same-service change can explain onset.

The 07:00Z order-service change (log.sampling_rate 0.1->0.2) is logging-only and on a different service off the portfolio path; the pre-window baseline 2026-03-09T18:00Z-06:00Z had zero changes, so the window contains exactly three changes total.
